name: Thymalin
used_for: A polypeptide extract from calf thymus developed by the Khavinson group in Russia and registered as a drug there, promoted online as an immune and anti-aging bioregulator. Evidence consists of Russian-language clinical reports, including a long follow-up of 266 older people with a control group from the originating institute, plus cell and animal studies. It is not approved by the FDA, and independent Western randomized evidence was not found. Its dipeptide components include Lys-Glu (KE), which is sold separately as Vilon.

internet_entries.text: A peptide wiki with affiliate discount codes says thymalin is commonly used at 10 mg intramuscularly or subcutaneously daily for 5 to 10 days, or a more conservative 5 mg daily for 10 days.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: An educational site (Peptides Institute, which carries no sales or affiliate links) says thymalin is given by intramuscular or subcutaneous injection in repeated courses, and that reconstituted powder is refrigerated, used within 5 to 7 days and never frozen.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: An educational site (Peptides Institute) lists injection-site reactions and transient fever as common effects, and rare allergic reactions and possible autoimmune flares in susceptible people as theoretical risks.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: An educational site (Peptides Institute) says thymalin supports immune restoration in aging, cites up to a 2-fold reduction in mortality in elderly subjects, and states that it is registered in Russia but not approved by the FDA or EMA.

research.summary: Russian-language report (Adv Gerontol) from the originating institutes following 266 older people for 6 to 8 years, with thymalin and epithalamin applied in the first 2 to 3 years, versus a control group.
research.finding: The authors report fewer acute respiratory infections and lower mortality in treated groups than controls. Report from the developers, with limited methodological detail, so it cannot be judged as independent controlled evidence.

research.summary: Cell-culture study (Bull Exp Biol Med) of thymalin on human hematopoietic stem cells.
research.finding: Thymalin lowered stem cell markers and raised CD28 expression, interpreted by the authors as promoting differentiation toward mature T lymphocytes. Cell data from the originating group.

research.summary: Rat study (Bull Exp Biol Med) of thymalin in rats with transplanted sarcoma.
research.finding: Low doses of thymalin were reported to arrest or regress tumor growth in more than half of animals. Animal data only.

research.summary: English-language report (Khavinson and Morozov, Neuro Endocrinol Lett) from the originating institutes on 266 older people followed for 6 to 8 years, with thymalin and epithalamin applied in the first 2 to 3 years, versus a control group.
research.finding: The authors report 2.0 to 2.1 times lower mortality in the thymalin group than in controls, and 4.1 times lower mortality in a separate group given thymalin plus epithalamin every year for 6 years. Developer report with limited methodological detail, not independent.

research.summary: Report (Khavinson et al., Stem Cell Rev Rep) of thymalin added to standard treatment in patients with COVID-19, compared with standard treatment alone. Group sizes and dosing are not stated in the abstract.
research.finding: Adding thymalin was reported to speed the fall in interleukin-6, C-reactive protein, D-dimer and T-cell markers. Lab markers only, from the originating group.

research.summary: Molecular modeling and cell study (Linkova, Khavinson et al., Int J Mol Sci) of the KE and EW dipeptides in thymalin, using blood cells from 4 donors.
research.finding: Thymalin and the two dipeptides lowered production of the inflammatory signals IL-1 beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha by 1.4 to 6.0 times in human blood cells exposed to a bacterial toxin. The docking results are computer predictions.

dose.summary: No trial dose was found. Online sources describe 5 to 10 mg per day by injection into muscle or under the skin for a short course. These doses are not backed by a study or label.

cycle_length.summary: In the developers' trial, thymalin was given during the first 2 to 3 years of a 6 to 8 year follow-up, and in one group every year for 6 years (with epithalamin). Online sources describe 5 to 10 day courses repeated every few months, which no study has tested.

items.text: In the developers' report on 266 older people, thymalin and epithalamin were applied in the first 2 to 3 years of a 6 to 8 year follow-up. One separate group got thymalin plus epithalamin every year for 6 years. Course length and dose per course are not given in the abstract.

mechanism.summary: Thought to act on the immune system by supplying thymus peptides and encouraging T cell development. How it works in people is not established; the evidence is from cell studies and computer modeling.

items.text: In human stem cell cultures, thymalin lowered stem cell markers and raised CD28, which the authors read as pushing cells toward mature T lymphocytes. Cell data from the originating group.
items.label: research

items.text: In human blood cells, thymalin and its KE and EW dipeptides lowered IL-1 beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha by 1.4 to 6.0 times. Binding to DNA was predicted by computer docking only.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptides Institute says thymalin supplies signaling peptides the aging thymus no longer makes enough of, binds DNA and histone proteins, supports T cell development and restores interleukin-2 production.
items.label: internet

best_documented_effect.summary: The developers report about half the mortality in older people treated with thymalin, over 6 to 8 years, but the report is not independent and lacks method detail. No independent controlled trial was found.

items.text: In 266 older people followed for 6 to 8 years, the authors report 2.0 to 2.1 times lower mortality and 2.0 to 2.4 times fewer acute respiratory infections in thymalin-treated groups than controls. Developer report, not independent.

side_effect_groups.summary: No human safety data was found. Peptides Institute lists injection-site reactions, brief fever, tiredness and headache as common.
